fish.name: Mud Darter
fish.flavor: Darts into the mud the instant it suspects it is being perceived. It is always being perceived.

fish.name: Meadow Minnow
fish.flavor: The pond's smallest optimist. Believes every ripple is a friend, which is statistically its biggest problem.

fish.name: Lilypad Sunny
fish.flavor: Suns itself beneath the lily pads with the quiet smugness of a cat that found the warm spot first.

fish.name: Speckled Pondloach
fish.flavor: Spends all day buried in the silt rehearsing what it would say if anyone ever dug it up. Nobody ever does.

fish.name: Duckweed Dace
fish.flavor: Wears a hat of duckweed at all times. Locals argue over whether it is camouflage or fashion. It is fashion.

fish.name: Rushwater Perch
fish.flavor: A dependable perch with sensible stripes. If the pond had a middle class, this fish would coach little league.

fish.name: Old Boot Bullhead
fish.flavor: Named for the boot it was found living in, which it defended with real conviction. The boot is now a local landmark.

fish.name: Cattail Chub
fish.flavor: Round, agreeable, and extremely fond of bread. Has personally attended every picnic held at this pond in living memory.

fish.name: Penny Roach
fish.flavor: Its scales shine like pocket change, and children swear catching one on your birthday grants a wish. The fish declines to comment.

fish.name: Dozing Bream
fish.flavor: Falls asleep mid-swim and drifts gently into things. The other fish have long since stopped pointing it out.

fish.name: Gossip Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Travels in tight schools where everyone knows everyone's business. Catch one, and the whole pond will hear about it by noon.

fish.name: Buttercup Tench
fish.flavor: Slick as butter and twice as hard to hold. Old-timers claim its slime cures hiccups, warts, and mild disappointment.

fish.name: Skipping Shiner
fish.flavor: Leaps clear of the water for no reason anyone has determined. Scientists say courtship display. The shiner says wheee.

fish.name: Mossback Crucian
fish.flavor: So patient that moss has begun to grow along its spine. It considers this a personal achievement.

fish.name: Dapple-Dawn Rudd
fish.flavor: Only bites while the light is doing that golden thing through the willows. Has better taste in mornings than most people.

fish.name: Picnic Bass
fish.flavor: Has learned the exact sound of a sandwich being unwrapped from forty feet away. Consider your lunch a shared resource.

fish.name: Willowshade Pike
fish.flavor: Lurks in the willow shadows wearing the expression of someone who has already decided which minnow it's having.

fish.name: Dewfin Smelt
fish.flavor: Its fins hold beads of morning dew long after sunrise. Handle gently; it is doing its very best.

fish.name: Grandma's Goldfish
fish.flavor: Released into the pond 'for its own good' three decades ago. It has since tripled in size and holds no grudges, probably.

fish.name: Stiltgrass Stickleback
fish.flavor: Builds a nest, guards it fiercely, and glares at anything that drifts within a fin's length. Three grams of pure principle.

fish.name: Clover Koi
fish.flavor: Its spots occasionally drift into a four-leaf pattern. Owning one is said to be lucky; catching one, the koi argues, is not.

fish.name: Bellringer Barbel
fish.flavor: Surfaces every evening at the exact moment the chapel bell rings. Nobody taught it this. The verger is quietly unnerved.

fish.name: Heron's Regret
fish.flavor: Too flat to grip and too spiny to swallow. The heron that tried still stands in the shallows, thinking about it.

fish.name: Mirrorbelly Carp
fish.flavor: Its belly reflects the sky so faithfully that landing one feels like pulling a piece of the afternoon out of the water.

fish.name: Sundial Loach
fish.flavor: Aligns itself with the sun and tells accurate time to anyone who can read a fish. So far that's one person, and she isn't sharing.

fish.name: Weathervane Eel
fish.flavor: Sleeps with its nose pointed toward tomorrow's weather. Farmers trust it over the almanac, the sky, and each other.

fish.name: Will-o'-the-Shallows
fish.flavor: A faint green light that drifts between the reeds on moonless nights. Follow it and you'll find nothing but the pond, which was perhaps the point.

fish.name: Thunderhead Catfish
fish.flavor: Rises an hour before every storm and stares at the sky like it's owed money. It has never once been wrong.

fish.name: Wedding Ring Perch
fish.flavor: Swallowed a gold ring in 1974 and has been engaged to the pond ever since. The groom married someone else. The perch is doing fine.

fish.name: The Millpond Matriarch
fish.flavor: Older than the mill, the miller, and the concept of milling hereabouts. When she passes beneath your boat, the water goes respectfully quiet.

fish.name: Whistlebone Gar
fish.flavor: Its hollow bones sound a low, sweet note as it swims. On still nights the whole pond hums a tune that nobody wrote.

fish.name: Lantern of the Lilies
fish.flavor: On midsummer nights it glows softly beneath the lily pads, and the frogs gather around it like parishioners. Nobody knows what it's promising them.

fish.name: Old Bellows
fish.flavor: Every generation swears they hooked him, and every generation's line snapped. The bubbles that rise from the deep hole by the drowned oak are, locals insist, him laughing.

fish.name: The Harvest Moon Koi
fish.flavor: Appears only when the harvest moon lies whole upon the water, swimming slow circles around its own reflection. Old couples come down to the bank just to watch, and don't say much.

fish.name: The Drowned Sun
fish.flavor: One perfect sunset sank into this pond and never came back up. On the finest evening of your life, your line will go heavy and warm, and the whole water will turn to gold around it.
